title: Modeling Book Sales Revenue as a Function of Price Increases
originalTopic: Theory and Examples: Applied Function Modeling
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Three hundred books sell for $40 each, generating a revenue of (300)($40) = $12,000. For each $5 increase in the unit price, 25 fewer books are sold. Express the total revenue R as a function of the number x of $5 price increases.

steps.title: Express the New Unit Price as a Function of x
steps.explanation: Starting from the base price of $40 per book, each of the x price increases adds $5 to the price, giving p(x) = 40 + 5x dollars per book.
steps.why: The unit price increases linearly by $5 per increment x.

steps.title: Express the Quantity Sold as a Function of x
steps.explanation: Starting from 300 books sold, each $5 increase reduces the number of books sold by 25, leaving q(x) = 300 - 25x books sold.
steps.why: Demand decreases linearly by 25 units per $5 price increase.

steps.title: Multiply Price and Quantity to Obtain Revenue R(x)
steps.explanation: Total revenue equals the number of books sold multiplied by the price per book: R(x) = (300 - 25x)(40 + 5x) = 12,000 + 500x - 125x^2.
steps.why: Total revenue is defined as the product of quantity sold and unit selling price.
